subject: Enclave observability handoff — SIEM export / tracehooks / evidence transfer
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 03 Dec 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Observability for private enclave — SIEM export questions

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for the demo last week. Our security team reviewed the private deployment notes and sent over a short list of requirements (attached). High-level asks:

- We need an outbound-only mechanism to get logs/traces/metrics into our Splunk (HEC) or an on-prem SIEM without creating inbound firewall holes.
- Support for mutual TLS or signed token auth is required; no plaintext syslog to open endpoints.
- Ability to strip/transform PII at the forwarder layer before leaving the VPC.
- Evidence bundles for audits that contain provenance (SHA256) and key rotation metadata.
- Tracing headers must preserve W3C traceparent so our distributed trace can stitch Redwood spans to our frontend.
- Retention and rotation: will accept 90/365 day retention guidance but need audit log entries for any export/transfer.

Can you confirm what options Redwood supports today and what would be in the handoff for an air-gapped/non-routed enclave? Also please include any schematic for the forwarder/service that runs in the enclave.

Best,
Samantha Ortiz
Head of Security Programs
Acme Health

Attachment: SIEM_requirements.pdf
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Cc: camila_reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Dec 2028 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Observability for private enclave — SIEM export questions

Samantha —

Thanks for the detailed list. Below is a concise handoff plan and options matrix; I attached a short design doc and an evidence checklist for the audit items you called out.

Summary of supported export patterns (enclave/private):

1) Outbound forwarder (recommended)
   - A lightweight forwarder runs in the customer enclave as a sidecar or dedicated DaemonSet.
   - Outbound-only connectivity: forwarder initiates TLS connections to customer-managed ingestion endpoints (HEC or HTTPS). No inbound ports required on the enclave.
   - Auth options: mTLS (mutual TLS with customer CA or Redwood-provisioned cert bundle), HEC token (rotatable), or signed JWT exchanged via a short-lived exchange.
   - Data handling: the forwarder applies configurable pipelines (Grok/regex/pipelining) and a transform step to remove or redact PII before transmission. Redaction rules are shipped as a versioned policy file.

2) Evidence escrow bundle (for audits / air-gapped handoffs)
   - When egress is not permitted, the forwarder can emit signed evidence bundles (tar.gz) to a customer-attested storage location (SFTP, removable media, or airgap export). Bundles contain: logs, trace snippets, metrics snapshots, manifest.json with SHA256 checksums, and a signature file.
   - We include key-rotation metadata in the manifest and an append-only audit file (rotation.log) that includes who/when keys rotated.

3) Metrics and tracing specifics
   - Metrics: Prometheus exposition locally + remote_write to customer remote-write endpoint; or push via a PushGateway that you own. We support batch compression and delta encoding to limit egress.
   - Tracing: We emit spans that contain W3C traceparent and tracestate headers. The forwarder preserves trace ids and can optionally sample at the edge (configurable policy) to limit volume.

Operational controls and observability hooks:
   - Audit trail: every forwarder action (publish, bundle created, key rotate) is logged locally with a UUID and stored for N days per your retention policy.
   - Health and telemetry: the forwarder exposes a read-only status endpoint (0auth-limited to the control plane) and emits internal metrics for delivery success/failure counts.

Next steps and handoff contents (what we will deliver):
   - enclave-forwarder-design-v1.md (attached)
   - evidence-transfer-checklist.csv (attached)
   - trace-hook-spec.md (attached)
   - A short runbook for firewall and proxy rules we need from your infra team

Security notes: we will not store customer raw keys in Redwood control plane for air-gapped flows; certs/tokens remain under customer custody unless you opt-in to us managing rotation.

If this looks right, I can loop in our compliance lead and produce a short checklist for your security reviewers.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Director, Product — Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
